description: Source-traced shared field-line schematic: preserve the central open B curves, flanking closed B_1 loops, all three double-loop E/E_1 groups, crossing structure, and each directional arrow. Pixel tracing anchors are not physical measurements. Native lower-right subscript glyphs are retained. This is not an exact space-time wave snapshot or proof of universal cancellation.

authoritativeText.text:
自然界的基本定律不仅归纳已经观察到的事实，还能在适用范围内预言新的现象。
麦克斯韦总结的电磁规律就是这样的例子。
如果每条定律只重复它所依据的事实，我们就需要为每一种现象单独建立一条规律。

科学定律的价值，正在于用相互联系的规律解释许多现象，并提出可以检验的预言。

从麦克斯韦的电磁场规律可以得出许多重要结论。
其中一个结论是：**电磁相互作用的变化以有限速度传播**，并不是瞬时传遍空间。

历史上的瞬时超距作用模型设想，一个电荷的位置改变后，另一个电荷所受的库仑力立即改变。
在这种描述中，电荷仿佛越过真空直接感受到远处电荷的变化，不需要传播时间。
库仑定律适用于静电情形。

不能把静电模型无条件用于运动电荷，并据此认为真实的相互作用变化也是瞬时传递的。

在麦克斯韦的场论中，电荷运动引起邻近电磁场的变化，场的扰动再向外传播。
随时间变化的电场与磁场，通过电磁场规律相互联系。
图中的分步叙述有助于理解这种联系。

但实际的电场和磁场是在空间与时间中共同变化的场，不能把它们理解成彼此独立、依次瞬时生成的物体。

图103是这种场联系的示意图。
变化的磁场以标为 $B$ 的磁感应线表示，与它相关的涡旋电场以标为 $E$ 的电场线表示。
电场的变化又与标为 $B_1$ 的磁场联系起来。

图中的曲线与箭头说明场线及其方向关系。
它不是某一实际波形在各个时刻的精确图像，也没有给出场强或传播距离的数值。

原书用新旧场在重叠区域中的相反方向，说明扰动向新的空间区域推进。
在图示的关系中，磁感应矢量 $\vec{B}$ 和 $\vec{B}_1$ 在同一区域的方向相反；
$\vec{E}$ 和 $\vec{E}_1$ 的方向关系也如此。

方向相反，并不意味着任意情形下两个场都完全抵消。
实际的场必须按电磁场规律共同求解，不能把示意图理解成旧场总会消失、而同样大小的新场总会取代它。

这些方向关系与第50节讨论的规律相联系。
由变化磁场产生的涡旋电场 $E$，和由变化电场联系到的磁场 $B$，不能随意用同一个方向规则替代各自的规律。
两种场关系的相对符号十分重要。

如果把它们改错，就可能得到无源区域中场能量凭空不断增长的错误结论，与能量守恒不相容。
这不是说实际电磁场会在一个区域无限增长，或在任意条件下都向所有方向均匀传播。

电荷位置的改变会引起电磁场扰动。
扰动向外传播时，会改变电荷移动前周围空间中存在的场。
扰动到达另一个电荷后，那个电荷所受的力才相应改变。

这不与第一个电荷移动的时刻同时发生。
麦克斯韦建立的场论说明了这种有限速度的传播，而不是要求电磁扰动通过机械介质传递。

麦克斯韦从电磁场规律推导出：电磁扰动在真空中的传播速度等于光在真空中的速度。
这里的真空条件不可省略，不能把这个速度无条件用于各种介质。
这一理论预言揭示了电磁场与光之间的重要联系。

它支持把场作为具有物理作用的对象来研究，但数学推导本身不能代替实验检验。

Fundamental laws of nature do more than summarize observations: within their domain of validity, they can predict new phenomena.

The electromagnetic laws formulated by Maxwell (麦克斯韦) are an example.

If each law merely repeated the observations on which it was based, a separate rule would be needed for every phenomenon.

Scientific laws are valuable because connected principles explain many phenomena and lead to predictions that can be tested.

Maxwell's (麦克斯韦) electromagnetic field laws lead to many important conclusions.

One is that **changes in electromagnetic interaction propagate at a finite speed**, rather than reaching all of space instantaneously.

In the historical model of instantaneous action at a distance, a change in one charge's position immediately changes the Coulomb force on another charge.

The charges are imagined to respond directly across the intervening vacuum, with no propagation time.
Coulomb's law applies to electrostatic situations.

It cannot be applied without qualification to moving charges to conclude that real changes in interaction are transmitted instantaneously.

In Maxwell's (麦克斯韦) field theory, motion of a charge changes the nearby electromagnetic field, and the disturbance propagates outward.

Time-varying electric and magnetic fields are linked by the electromagnetic field laws.
A step-by-step diagram helps illustrate this connection.

The actual electric and magnetic fields evolve together in space and time;
they are not separate objects created one after another instantaneously.

Figure 103 is a schematic of these field relationships.

The changing magnetic field is represented by field lines labeled $B$, and the associated circulating electric field by lines labeled $E$.

Changes in the electric field are in turn linked to the magnetic field labeled $B_1$.
The curves and arrows show field lines and their directional relationships.

They are not exact snapshots of a particular wave at successive times, and they supply no numerical field strengths or propagation distances.

The original textbook uses opposing directions of old and newly induced fields in overlapping regions to illustrate the disturbance advancing into new regions of space.

In the relationship shown, the magnetic induction vectors $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{B}_1$ point in opposite directions in the same region;

the directional relationship between $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{E}_1$ is similar.
Opposite directions do not mean that the two fields cancel completely in every situation.

The actual fields must be solved together using the electromagnetic field laws;

the schematic does not imply that an old field always disappears and is replaced by an equally strong new field.

These directional relationships are connected to the laws discussed in Section 50.

The circulating electric field $E$ associated with a changing magnetic field, and the magnetic field $B$ associated with a changing electric field, cannot have their respective laws replaced arbitrarily by the same direction rule.

The relative signs of the two field relationships matter.

Using incorrect signs can lead to an unphysical prediction of field energy growing without a source, contrary to energy conservation.

This does not mean that actual electromagnetic fields grow without limit in one region or propagate uniformly in every direction under all conditions.

A change in a charge's position produces an electromagnetic field disturbance.

As the disturbance propagates outward, it changes the field that existed around the charge before the motion.

The force on another charge changes in response when the disturbance reaches it, not at the same instant as the first charge moves.

Maxwell's (麦克斯韦) field theory describes this finite-speed propagation;
it does not require electromagnetic disturbances to travel through a mechanical medium.

Maxwell (麦克斯韦) derived from the electromagnetic field laws that the speed of electromagnetic disturbances in vacuum equals the speed of light in vacuum.

The vacuum condition is essential;
the same speed cannot be assumed for every material medium.

This theoretical prediction revealed an important connection between electromagnetic fields and light.

It supports studying the field as a physical entity with observable effects, but mathematical derivation alone does not replace experimental testing.

inventory.description: Two upright OPEN magnetic-field curves flank the central horizontal field-line group. The left curve extends from about (199,19), bows right toward (238,168), and continues to about (210,307). The right curve extends from about (348,23), bows left toward (307,168), and continues to about (331,317). Both top arrowheads point upward/outward. Keep both full lower endpoints; neither curve is a closed ellipse. The centered top label is B.

Two upright CLOSED, noncircular elongated loops: one at the left, roughly x109..185 and y56..291, and one at the right, roughly x365..444 and y56..286. The left loop's right branch points downward and its left branch points upward. The right loop's left branch points downward and its right branch points upward. Both upper labels are B with a lower-right subscript 1. Retain the opposing branch directions, crossing locations, and the closed versus open distinction from the central B curves.

Two flattened horizontal closed electric-field loops on the left, not circles: outer extent approximately x13..205, y141..208; inner extent approximately x41..183, y154..197. Each has an upper-branch arrow pointing right and a lower-branch arrow pointing left. Keep the leftmost endpoints, the right-side overlap with the center group, and the E label with subscript 1 above-left.

Two flattened horizontal closed electric-field loops in the center. The outer curve spans approximately x165..394, y140..216; the inner curve spans approximately x212..329, y157..193. Each upper branch points right and each lower branch points left. The E label is near the lower-left portion of this central group, in the printed gap; retain association with this group rather than relabeling it E1.

Two flattened horizontal closed electric-field loops on the right, outer extent approximately x351..543, y141..214 and inner extent approximately x382..515, y153..197. Each upper branch points right and each lower branch points left. Retain the rightmost extent, overlap with the center group, and the upper-right E label with subscript 1.

One shared white-background schematic, with three overlapping horizontal groups and upright magnetic curves crossing them. There is no axis, coordinate grid, measurement, equal-interval claim, scale, caption within the crop, or separate-panel boundary. Keep the shared geometry, all 18 observed directional arrowheads, the six labels and all four subscript-1 glyphs. Printed line gaps at crossings/labels must not be turned into missing loops or new physical endpoints.
